# Trustworthy Local Document Intelligence — Stage 1

A fully-offline system for an Apple M1 (8 GB) that answers questions over 16 long statistical PDFs
and verifies factual claims against them.

**Numbers are never generated by the language model.** The model selects which table cells and
which operation; a Python function does the arithmetic and returns the value. Every answer carries
a citation — `{doc, page}` for prose, `{doc, page, table_id, cell}` for numbers.

Results in one line: **11/20 on the development gold set, 8/9 on a held-out set of unseen
documents.** Those numbers are not comparable — see [Known limitations](#7-known-limitations)
before reading either as a capability claim.

> **Stage 2** (LoRA fine-tuning on Qwen2.5-**3B**, and the three-arm comparison) is documented
> separately in **[STAGE2_README.md](STAGE2_README.md)**, with `MEMO_STAGE2.md` as its write-up.
> Sections 1–5 below are a prerequisite for it: Stage 2 needs the same environment, corpus and
> index. Stage 2's results reproduce in ~25 minutes **without** retraining.

---

## 1. Prerequisites

| requirement | detail |
|---|---|
| hardware | **Apple Silicon Mac** (M1 or later). Built and measured on a base M1 MacBook Air |
| memory | **8 GB unified minimum.** 8 GB is the practical floor, not a comfortable target — see §7 |
| macOS | Any version with Metal support (built on macOS 15 / Darwin 24.6) |
| Python | **3.11.** Not the macOS system `python3` |
| disk | **~14 GB free**: 4 GB model + 0.2 GB embedding model + 39 MB corpus + ~1 GB indices, plus headroom |
| network | Needed **only** for setup (model + corpus download). The pipeline itself runs offline |

**The Python version bites people.** The macOS system `python3` is often 3.7, which `mlx-lm`
rejects (needs ≥3.9). Check before you start:

```bash
python3 --version     # if this says 3.7.x, you MUST use the conda env below
```

---

## 2. Environment setup

From a blank terminal:

```bash
git clone git@github.com:Diamante2728/local-document-intelligence.git
cd local-document-intelligence

conda create -y -n doc-intel python=3.11
conda activate doc-intel
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

Takes ~4 minutes. All versions are pinned to what this build was measured on, and this exact
sequence was verified from a clean clone into an empty environment.

---

## 3. Download the model and verify your setup

```bash
python -c "from mlx_lm import load; load('mlx-community/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-4bit')"
```

~4 GB, one-time, a few minutes on a normal connection. Cached in `~/.cache/huggingface/`.

**A second model downloads automatically on first ingestion** — `BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5`
(~130 MB), used for embeddings. You do not need to fetch it manually, but it explains an
unexpected download the first time you run §5.

**Verify the setup — this is the Phase 0 offline proof.** `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1` makes
`huggingface_hub` refuse every network call, so if this generates text, the pipeline genuinely
runs offline:

```bash
python -c "import mlx.core as mx; print('device:', mx.default_device())"
# expect: device: Device(gpu, 0)

HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 python -c "
from mlx_lm import load, generate
m, t = load('mlx-community/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-4bit')
print(generate(m, t, prompt=t.apply_chat_template(
    [{'role':'user','content':'What is the capital of France?'}], add_generation_prompt=True),
    max_tokens=20, verbose=False))
"
# expect a sentence naming Paris, ~10-20s
```

Expect **~9 tokens/sec warm** and **~4.4 GB peak** on a base M1. The first call in any process is
much slower — that is Metal shader compilation, not throughput.

---

## 4. Fetch the corpus

```bash
python download_corpus.py
```

16 public PDFs (FDIC, BEA ×3, Census ×3, Federal Reserve ×2, USDA ×2, OECD, Treasury, World Bank,
EPA, EIA) — **~39 MB, 713 pages, about 3 minutes.** Every URL is a dated archive link, verified to
return a real PDF. The PDFs are gitignored; this script is the reproducible source of truth.

---

## 5. Build the index

```bash
python -m src.ingest.run_ingest
```

**Takes ~20 minutes on an M1** and prints per-document progress. It extracts prose chunks and
tables, repairs tables whose row labels were dropped, verifies stored cells against the source
page text, and builds the two FAISS indices. Output: `index/` (~1 GB) and a written report at
`results/ingestion_check.md`.

Expected tail:

```
Verifying stored cells against source page text...
Building table retrieval index...
  table retrieval index: kept 260, skipped 679 as non-numeric/too-small
Wrote .../results/ingestion_check.md
```

Everything after this point runs with the network off. Prefix any command with
`HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1` to prove it.

---

## 6. Running the system

### Ask a question (deliverable 1A)

```bash
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 python -m src.qa.ask \
  "What was the noncurrent loan rate for construction and development loans at all insured institutions?"
```

Expected shape — note the number is *computed*, and the citation resolves to a specific cell:

```
A: 0.6
   (computed in Python: operation=lookup)

path: numeric  |  confidence: 0.689  |  131.70s
citations:
  - fdic_quarterly_banking_profile_2024q1 p13 p13_t0 r23c1
```

Numeric questions take **60–170 s**; prose questions **20–40 s**. That is expected on this
hardware — the evaluation is about method, not speed.

Other paths:

```bash
# prose
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 python -m src.qa.ask "By how much did real GDP increase in the first quarter of 2024?"
# multi-doc
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 python -m src.qa.ask "Compare the homeownership rate with the official poverty rate."
```

Flags: `--json` for machine-readable output, `--no-llm-router` for deterministic rules-only
routing (used by the benchmark so routing noise cannot confound results).

### Verification layer (deliverable 1C)

```bash
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 python -m src.verify.score
```

Verifies the 15 claims in `summary.md`, writes `results/verification_report.md` with
precision/recall, a 3-way confusion matrix and a per-claim table. **Takes ~15 minutes.**

> **This command will fail in a fresh clone, by design.** It decrypts `answer_key.enc` at eval
> time, and the key that decrypts it is deliberately not committed — the planted-error answers are
> meant to stay hidden until the walkthrough. You will get an explicit `MissingSecret` error
> explaining this. To run it against your own key, write a plaintext `answer_key.json` and run
> `python -m src.verify.keystore encrypt answer_key.json answer_key.enc`, which generates a secret
> for you. The committed `results/verification_report.md` contains the full results from the
> original run.

Re-render the report from the last run without re-running the model:

```bash
python -m src.verify.score --from-cache
```

### Benchmark and the quantization ladder (deliverable 1D)

```bash
python -m src.quant.kv_math                          # instant, no model load
python -m src.quant.bench --limit 2 --label smoke    # ~2 min, proves the harness works
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 python -m src.quant.bench --label int4    # full 20 questions, ~45 min
python -m src.quant.bench --holdout --label holdout  # 9 held-out questions, ~10 min
python -m src.quant.report                           # regenerate results/quant_table.md
```

`--resume` continues an interrupted run from its checkpoint; `--fresh` restarts. Use `--limit N`
or `--type numeric` for quick checks rather than waiting for a full run.

To reproduce the INT8 memory wall (it will fail — that is the finding):

```bash
python -m src.quant.ladder fetch-int8    # ~7.5 GB download
python -m src.quant.ladder try-int8      # loads, then Metal OOM
```

## 7. Repo map

```
MEMO.md                      2-page memo — the main analytical write-up
PROGRESS.md                  phase-by-phase completion checklist
AI_LOG.md                    running log of assistant use + errors it made (required disclosure)
gold_set.json                20 development questions (8 prose, 8 numeric, 4 multi-doc)
holdout_set.json             9 held-out questions on 7 documents never used in development
summary.md                   15 analyst claims, 6 of them deliberately wrong
answer_key.enc               encrypted answer key — INTENTIONALLY encrypted, not broken (see §6)
download_corpus.py           fetches the 16-PDF corpus

src/ingest/                  PDF -> SQLite + FAISS: parsing, table repair, cell verification
src/qa/                      router, prose path, numeric plan->compute path, multi-doc, CLI
src/verify/                  claim verification, scoring, Fernet keystore
src/quant/                   KV/weight arithmetic, measurement, benchmark, ladder, reporting

results/
  quant_table.md             deliverable 1D — the three rungs, with the INT8/FP16 mechanism
  verification_report.md     deliverable 1C — precision/recall + confusion matrix
  multidoc_failure_analysis.md   every multi-doc failure categorised with evidence
  fix_attempt_analysis.md    four fixes, net-zero result, and where the bottleneck actually is
  known_limitations.md       L0-L6, the durable caveat list
  kv_math.md                 KV-cache arithmetic from the model's real config
  ingestion_check.md         per-document extraction stats + full breakage log
```

Not committed (rebuildable or secret): `corpus/*.pdf`, `index/`, model weights,
`answer_key.json`, `.answer_key_secret`.

---

## 8. Known limitations

Stated upfront rather than left to be discovered. Full analysis in
[`MEMO.md`](MEMO.md) and [`results/known_limitations.md`](results/known_limitations.md).

**8 GB is the floor, and INT8/FP16 will not run.** Not a configuration you can tune — INT8 needs
7.6 GB of weights against MLX's own stated 5.46 GB maximum, and was measured to load and then die
at the Metal layer during generation. FP16 needs 15.2 GB, more than the machine has. Details and
arithmetic in [`results/quant_table.md`](results/quant_table.md).

**Numeric accuracy is the weakest question type** (4/8 on the gold set). Failures are cell
*selection*, not retrieval — measurement showed the correct cell was already in the model's context
in all four misses.

**Multi-doc is weak** (1/4 gold, 0/1 held-out). Two of the four failures are the model declining
facts that were in its context; the mechanism for each is documented in
[`results/multidoc_failure_analysis.md`](results/multidoc_failure_analysis.md).

**The two accuracy numbers are not comparable.** The held-out set (8/9) contains **zero numeric
questions** — it is 8 prose + 1 multi-doc, so it omits the type the system scores worst on. Do not
read 0.889 as general capability, and do not read 0.55 as the system's ceiling on prose.

**The confidence score is not calibrated.** It measures how an answer was produced (retrieval
agreement, which code path ran), never whether it is right. Observed directly: one answer scored
**0.753 while wrong**, and after a fix the same question scored **0.689 while right**.

**Two rounds of improvements produced no net accuracy gain** (11/20 → 11/20), with a citation-rate
regression from 1.00 to 0.90. That result and its diagnosis are in
[`results/fix_attempt_analysis.md`](results/fix_attempt_analysis.md).
